result.title: EvoSearch: Self-Evolving Active Perception for Wide-Area Geospatial Search
result.summary: Geospatial search is fundamental to resource surveys and environmental monitoring, requiring the discovery of relevant evidence across large geographic areas and multiple spatial scales. Existing active perception methods adaptively select observation locations and scales to improve search efficiency, yet their search trajectories become increasingly long and costly as the search area expands. A key limitation is that final-answer correctness alone provides little guidance on which observations to retain and when to stop, hindering efficient wide-area search. To address this challenge, we propose EvoSearch, a self-evolving active perception framework that co-evolves the perception policy and exploration program to compress search trajectories while preserving answer quality. Specifically, quality-cost comparisons between completed branches from shared evidence train the policy to acquire useful observations, avoid redundant ones, and stop when sufficient evidence is available. Execution feedback from the updated policy then guides exploration-program revision, adapting experience generation to the policy's changing observation needs. We further introduce GeoSearchBench, a benchmark for evaluating search quality and visual processing efficiency through relational search and region search. Experiments demonstrate that EvoSearch shortens search trajectories and substantially reduces visual processing while maintaining overall search quality, supporting scalable active perception for wide-area geospatial search.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoSearch 自演化主动感知框架，联合优化感知策略与探索程序，利用已完成分支的质量—成本比较学习保留有用观测、避免冗余并在证据充分时停止，同时构建 GeoSearchBench 评估搜索质量与视觉处理效率。
